speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic; I'm Dr. Agent. To understand your gait and limb ataxia, could you tell me if you have any family history of similar neurological conditions or known genetic disorders? Also, when did you first notice these walking difficulties?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the "drunk" appearance and right-sided predominance are significant clues. Have you noticed any changes in your speech, vision, or swallowing difficulties alongside these motor symptoms? Also, do you have any history of cancer or exposure to heavy metals like mercury or arsenic?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and natalizumab use, I need to rule out progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML). REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with and without contrast. REQUEST TEST: JC Virus PCR. Also, have you noticed any new visual changes, numbness, or weakness in the past few months?

Comments: T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML. JC Virus PCR: Not reported in data. Symptoms: Ataxic gait, Right Upper Limb Strength 4/5, Evidence of ataxia.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. The MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement, combined with your history of Crohn's disease and natalizumab use, along with symptoms of ataxia and weakness, confirm this diagnosis. We need to immediately discontinue natalizumab and consider switching to a safer biologic for your Crohn's.
